title: Daily Market Digest - August 1, 2026
subtitle: Markets Closed for Weekend; Review of Friday, July 31, 2026 Session

items.headline: Tech Rally Leads U.S. Stocks Higher on Friday; Inflation Concerns Persist
items.summary: U.S. equities concluded a volatile July with a broad rally on Friday, July 31, driven by strong tech earnings and renewed optimism around AI. Major indices posted gains, but rising Treasury yields and persistent inflation worries continued to weigh on sentiment. Markets are closed today, Saturday, August 1, 2026. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Amazon Soars on Strong Earnings and AI Bets
items.summary: Amazon ($AMZN) jumped after reporting stronger-than-expected second-quarter profits, with robust growth in Amazon Web Services (AWS) suggesting its significant AI investments are yielding returns.

items.headline: Alphabet Climbs Amid Broader Tech Rally
items.summary: Alphabet ($GOOGL) saw solid gains as technology stocks rebounded strongly, buoyed by positive sentiment around AI and strong performances from other tech giants.

items.headline: Microsoft Continues Momentum Post-Earnings
items.summary: Microsoft ($MSFT) extended its gains, building on Thursday's massive surge driven by robust quarterly results and an upbeat forecast for its Azure cloud business.

items.headline: Reddit Plunges on Heavy Selling Volume
items.summary: Reddit ($RDDT) experienced a significant sell-off, collapsing on substantial institutional trading volume and closing near its annual lows.

items.headline: Apple Drops on Muted Revenue Outlook
items.summary: Apple ($AAPL) shares fell following a lackluster forecast for upcoming revenue growth, with investor concerns arising from disappointing Q4 guidance, rising component costs, and slowing growth in key segments.

items.headline: Micron Technology Falls Amid Mixed Chip Sector Performance
items.summary: Micron Technology ($MU) was among the decliners, as memory-focused semiconductor names lagged despite a generally positive day for the broader chip sector.

items.headline: Fed Holds Rates Steady, Dallas Fed President Logan Dissents
items.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rates, as widely expected. However, Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan dissented, advocating for a 0.25 percentage point rate increase, citing persistent inflation that appears to be trending toward the mid-2s rather than the 2% target.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Climb on Inflation Concerns
items.summary: Treasury yields rose on Friday, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury note surging above 4.7%. Worries about inflation remaining high continued to build in the bond market.

items.headline: Employment Cost Index Rises; Jobless Claims Increase
items.summary: The Employment Cost Index (ECI) for June 2026 showed civilian worker compensation costs increasing 0.9% in the second quarter, driven by a 0.9% rise in wages and salaries and a 1.0% increase in benefit costs. Meanwhile, initial jobless claims for the week ending July 25 totaled 197,000, an increase of 9,000 from the prior week.

items.headline: Tech and Consumer Discretionary Lead Gains; Energy Strong
items.summary: Technology and Consumer Discretionary sectors were the strongest performers, largely benefiting from strong earnings reports from mega-cap tech companies and renewed AI optimism. The Energy sector also showed robust performance, reflecting elevated oil prices. Conversely, the Health Care sector reported a year-over-year decline in earnings.

items.headline: Major Companies Report Q2 Results: ExxonMobil and Chevron Post Strong Earnings
items.summary: ExxonMobil ($XOM) announced Q2 2026 earnings of $14.5 billion, or $3.48 per share. Chevron ($CVX) reported Q2 2026 earnings of $12.1 billion, or $6.11 per share diluted, driven by record U.S. production and refinery throughput. FactSet forecasts S&P 500 earnings growth at 24.7% for Q2 2026.

items.headline: Rising Oil Prices and AI Investments Drive Macro Narrative
items.summary: Rising oil prices, fueled by renewed Middle East tensions, contributed to ongoing inflation concerns. Meanwhile, continued massive investments in Artificial Intelligence infrastructure are increasingly seen as a key driver for cloud demand and tech sector growth.
